papers.canonical_title: GREP: Grounding Generated Room Evaluation in Principles
papers.abstract: GREP evaluates generated furnished rooms through physical validity, visual coherence and human-use logic. An evaluation agent discovers scene-specific checks, gathers geometric and visual evidence, and produces scores and diagnostic reports. It reports 86.7% agreement with human majority preferences and improved report-guided scene refinement.
papers.screening_reason: The evaluation agent selects scene-specific checks and camera observations, executing measurement and rendering operations on generated 3D rooms. This is interactive graphics auditing, not merely a passive quality score.
screening_evidence: Sections 3.1–3.3 and Appendix A describe autonomous check discovery and evidence acquisition on fixed room geometry.
Appendix C.3 identifies Blender EEVEE rendering; Appendix E separately demonstrates report-guided layout revision.
papers.analysis_target: GREP task-time evaluation/inspection agent, including check discovery, scoped evidence acquisition and adjudication; not the separate benchmark generation agents or GPT-4.1 refinement experiment.

agent_graphics_relation.controller: VLM evaluation agent with discovery, metric evaluator and camera-selection components
agent_graphics_relation.action_or_decision: Formulates checks, requests spatial measurements and selects/revises rendered camera views
agent_graphics_relation.graphics_target: Generated furnished 3D room geometry, camera state and evidence views
agent_graphics_relation.evidence: The evaluator requests additional evidence; the camera selector supplies views while scene geometry remains fixed.

task.evidence: Evaluates room assets, positions, orientations and scales.
task.reasoning: Audits static scene modeling quality; no dynamics authoring. Task label is purpose, while Auditing is the operation.

input_form.evidence: Submitted assets, geometry, transforms and scene context initialize evaluation.
input_form.reasoning: Task input is a 3D scene; internally rendered images are feedback, not an additional input modality.

output.evidence: Inspection records identify check type, objects, verdict, reason, evidence and decision source.
output.reasoning: Structured diagnostic report is the exposed product; rendered probes are intermediate evidence.

model_type.evidence: VLM inspects scene views and GPT-5.6 Sol supplies judgments.

model_training.locator: Sections 3–4; Appendix C; full-text training/fine-tuning search
model_training.evidence: Deployment configuration is described but no explicit adaptation or no-training statement is provided for the evaluator.
model_training.reasoning: Named commercial model alone is insufficient to establish Off-the-Shelf under the annotation policy.

planning.evidence: Discovery instantiates object-specific checks from fixed types, with predefined evidence requirements supplemented by model observation goals.
planning.reasoning: Explicit check/evidence plan combines fixed schema with adaptive targets and requests.

workflow.evidence: Metric-specific branches resolve conclusive cases or acquire evidence; checks share scoped evidence and may omit components.
workflow.reasoning: Substantive conditional paths and per-metric dependencies support graph-structured execution.

update_strategy.evidence: Camera candidates are generated and filtered, then selected to cover missing observations; VLM repair proposals are bounded.
update_strategy.reasoning: Feedback changes selected evidence views, not room geometry. Candidate selection is supported; no claim of scene patching in evaluator.

verifier.evidence: Deterministic gate tests usable image files; metric evaluator judges whether observations resolve the check.
verifier.reasoning: Self denotes evaluator judging its inspection evidence; programmatic gate controls evidence acceptance.

feedback_assessment.evidence: Evidence sufficiency and unmet observation requirements determine requests for more views.
feedback_assessment.reasoning: Binary sufficiency plus diagnostic missing-feature requests guide further acquisition. Final scene scores are not this loop's Score feedback.

feedback_observation.evidence: Views, distance, angle, overlap and clearance form evidence packets.
feedback_observation.reasoning: Rendered views are Visual; geometry/pose measurements are Structural Scene State.

memory_time.evidence: Views acquired for one check are retained for later checks within the same scope.
memory_time.reasoning: Retained evidence spans calls in one evaluation, not demonstrated across independent runs.

memory_reach.evidence: Function checks share a group evidence bank; other metrics use their own scopes.
memory_reach.reasoning: Scope-limited sharing is local, not a single globally accessible memory.

action_type.evidence: Agent selects measurement, view retrieval and additional rendering operations.
action_type.reasoning: Callable evidence operations are the action interface.

graphics_software.evidence: Dedicated measurement/camera interface uses Blender EEVEE for evidence rendering.
graphics_software.reasoning: Agent-facing inspection layer adapts a general graphics engine.

tools.evidence: Camera/render operations and geometric screening are used during inspection.
tools.reasoning: Camera changes/rendering are Graphics Operations; geometric feasibility and evidence-file checks are Static Validator. No physical solver is executed.

resources.evidence: Asset geometry/catalog usable-side references and fixed evidence/check rules inform evaluation.
resources.reasoning: Reusable meshes/catalog data support Assets; prescribed evaluation rules support Documentation & Rules.

representation.evidence: Asset meshes and scene transforms are measured and rendered into evidence images.
representation.reasoning: Geometry and Pixels both participate in the evaluator; report schema is not graphics Code.

papers.contribution: Principle-grounded adaptive room inspection links geometric and visual evidence to object-level diagnoses instead of relying on fixed views or predeclared questions.
papers.limitations: Human agreement uses 15 dependent pairs from six scenes and five researchers. Judge-family bias remains possible. Bounded acquisition can force verdicts or default-valid outcomes; complete judgment coverage does not imply complete issue discovery. Refinement uses a distinct scoring protocol and only five scenes.
taxonomy_delta: Modeling is used for static-scene quality auditing; current task labels lack an explicit inspection/auditing task, which is instead preserved in operations.
Memory uses scope-local retained evidence; source Working Memory terminology remains ambiguous but is not needed here.

papers.canonical_title: Clips2Story: Training-Free Video Storyboarding and Editing Using Multimodal Retrieval-Embedded Generation
papers.abstract: A training-free LLM pipeline retrieves clips relevant to a keyword, plans an editable storyboard with connective narration, and assembles a video from fragmented footage. Evaluated on shuffled clips from 100 long-form videos.
papers.screening_reason: LLM editorial decisions select, trim and order actual video assets through an executable JSON storyboard. A fixed one-pass pipeline still establishes agent-to-graphics decisions; no iterative feedback is claimed.
screening_evidence: Section 3.4 and Appendix C specify clip IDs, temporal bounds and narration used for final assembly.
papers.analysis_target: Task-time Clips2Story-ND editorial planner and its retrieval/assembly harness; excludes dataset-construction LLM, NF ablation, optional human prototype editing and final evaluation.

agent_graphics_relation.action_or_decision: Selects, trims and sequences clip IDs and connective narration in JSON
agent_graphics_relation.graphics_target: Editable video timeline and assembled audiovisual media
agent_graphics_relation.evidence: Ordered segment specifications determine which footage appears and its start/end times.

task.evidence: Composes keyword-directed short videos through temporal sequencing.
task.reasoning: Temporal media authoring is closest to Animation, not 3D modeling; video-editing boundary noted in delta.

input_form.evidence: Pool of clips and user keyword are task inputs.
input_form.reasoning: Video supplies footage; Language specifies topic. Extracted captions are internal representations.

output.evidence: Editable JSON storyboard and final assembled video are exposed.
output.reasoning: JSON is Structured Specification; video is Rendered Media.

model_type.evidence: GPT-5.2 receives textual multimodal descriptors for timeline planning.
model_type.reasoning: Decision-maker is a text LLM; BLIP perception does not make the controller Hybrid.

planning.evidence: LLM creates story plan under fixed schema, duration and transcript-boundary constraints.
planning.reasoning: Explicit generated timeline within fixed retrieval/assembly stages is hybrid PO-2.

workflow.evidence: Descriptor extraction, retrieval, storyboard generation, narration/visual selection, final assembly.
workflow.reasoning: ND follows a fixed ordered path; NF is an alternative configuration, not runtime branching.

update_strategy.evidence: No autonomous revise-after-execution loop is described.
update_strategy.reasoning: Initial clip selection is not a response to feedback; update strategy does not apply to this one-pass planner.

verifier.evidence: Metrics and participant ratings evaluate completed results; prototype human edits are separate.
verifier.reasoning: No verifier changes later planner actions in analyzed automated configuration.

feedback_assessment.evidence: VTGHLS ranks footage for narration, while other scores are final evaluations.
feedback_assessment.reasoning: Retrieval scoring is initial assembly, not a revision feedback loop; Not Applicable rather than Score.

feedback_observation.evidence: Planner sees descriptors but no resulting rendering is fed back.
feedback_observation.reasoning: Task conditioning is not loop feedback.

memory_time.evidence: Metadata extracted once per input video can be reused across different editing prompts.
memory_time.reasoning: Explicit reuse across separate editing requests supports persistent content memory, not experience learning.

memory_reach.evidence: Clip descriptors are reused by retrieval and planner in this editorial pipeline.
memory_reach.reasoning: A pipeline-scoped content store is Local; no multi-agent globally shared memory asserted.

action_type.evidence: Strict JSON containing narration and clip_id/start_time/end_time segments.

graphics_software.evidence: Custom JSON storyboards drive footage assembly and narration rendering.
graphics_software.reasoning: Dedicated agent-facing declarative adapter, not direct native editor GUI.

tools.evidence: WhisperX, BLIP, GroundingDINO and CLIP extract descriptors; assembly trims/sequences footage.
tools.reasoning: Perception models analyze inputs; Graphics Operations materialize temporal edits.

resources.evidence: Retrieves candidate clips and supplies fixed editing rules.
resources.reasoning: Reusable footage is Assets; prompt constraints are Documentation & Rules.

representation.evidence: Existing video frames are selected and assembled without 3D geometry.
representation.reasoning: Pixels represent graphics content; JSON temporal plan is not executable code or 2D layout.

papers.contribution: Turns unordered footage into keyword-directed editable narrative plans rather than preserving the chronology of a source video.
papers.limitations: Text descriptors miss fine visual/audio continuity; hard retrieval may discard useful B-roll; generated storylines can misleadingly recontextualize factual footage. Duration overshoot and repeated narration visuals remain. Evaluation uses shuffled single-source videos, not arbitrary real multi-source repositories.
taxonomy_delta: Animation is the nearest task label for temporal video editing; no animated geometry is authored.
Persistent descriptor reuse is content memory, not cross-run learned design expertise.

papers.canonical_title: An Agentic Framework for Quality-Aware and Scenario-Adaptive Image Compression
papers.abstract: PICA coordinates perception, pre-coding restoration, codec quality control and post-coding restoration through scenario-guided quality-rate feedback. Agentic ROI Coding adapts black-box codecs without retraining.
papers.screening_reason: VLM agents explicitly schedule restoration tools and ROI coding plans that modify pixel artifacts using measured feedback.
screening_evidence: III.C–D pp.5–8: generate candidate restoration/coding plans, execute, evaluate, retain or reschedule.
papers.analysis_target: PICA task-time four-agent restoration/compression harness, default Qwen3-VL-8B controller; not codec training or downstream detection evaluation.

agent_graphics_relation.action_or_decision: Invokes restoration tools and chooses regional quality-control/downsampling plans
agent_graphics_relation.graphics_target: Input and reconstructed raster image regions
agent_graphics_relation.evidence: AROIC executes scheduled ROI/background codec plans, evaluates reconstructions, and reschedules unsuccessful plans.

task.reasoning: None of Modeling/Animation/Simulation/Visualization clearly denotes image coding; preserve task ambiguity rather than invent mapping.

input_form.evidence: Observed image and user compression instruction initialize PICA.

output.evidence: Outputs aggregate coded representation and reconstructed image.
output.reasoning: Encoded raster artifact and restored image, not executable program or animation.

model_type.evidence: Qwen3-VL supports planning, tool invocation and feedback-guided refinement across agents.

model_training.evidence: Explicit training-free framework uses pretrained models without additional training.

planning.evidence: Schedules restoration subtasks and ROI coding plans inside fixed four-agent stages.
planning.reasoning: Generated plans within fixed scaffolding support PO-2.

workflow.evidence: Perception then improvement then coding then after-coding improvement, each with internal iteration.
workflow.reasoning: Ordered stage path; candidate plurality does not establish parallel execution.

update_strategy.evidence: Retains best candidates and refines remaining restoration or ROI plans on failure.
update_strategy.reasoning: Best-candidate choice is Candidate Selection; changed remaining plan is Replanning. Baseline retention is not necessarily rollback.

verifier.evidence: Agent reflects on outcome; SGQR and quality/bitrate thresholds control acceptance.
verifier.reasoning: Self reflection plus deterministic metric/threshold tests guide subsequent actions.

feedback_assessment.evidence: SGQR cost, acceptance criteria, and actionable bitrate/quality feedback guide rescheduling.
feedback_assessment.reasoning: Cost is Score; pass/fail is Binary; unmet-constraint explanation is Diagnosis.

feedback_observation.evidence: Reconstructed images are reassessed for residual degradation and perceptual quality.
feedback_observation.reasoning: Visual artifact evidence informs decisions; numeric bitrate is not a runtime execution error.

memory_time.evidence: Current best image, baseline setting and remaining plan persist through iterations.
memory_time.reasoning: Run-local retained candidates and plan support Short-Term Memory, no cross-run learning claimed.

memory_reach.evidence: Each subtask holds its reference and selected candidate; stages pass output images.
memory_reach.reasoning: Stage-local retained state is evidenced; globally accessible store is not.

action_type.evidence: Controller performs tool invocation for restoration and codec execution.

graphics_software.evidence: Unified QC interface wraps VTM and CompressAI codecs with ROI crop/reassembly.
graphics_software.reasoning: New agent adapter layer around existing software.

tools.evidence: Restoration/IQA networks, crop/downsample/codec operations and threshold checks execute in loops.
tools.reasoning: Networks are Perception models; raster operations are Graphics Operations; deterministic acceptance is Static Validator.

resources.evidence: Codec-specific high-level QC knowledge guides initialization.
resources.reasoning: Reusable parameter rules, not new asset libraries or evaluation datasets.

representation.evidence: Image arrays, ROI crops and reconstructed raster pixels are operated on.

papers.contribution: Codec-agnostic regional compression and restoration decisions jointly optimize scenario-specific quality and bitrate without retraining codecs.
papers.limitations: Evidence covers two codecs and synthetically added Gaussian noise/defocus blur on relatively small image sets. No dedicated limitations section or runtime-cost accounting was found; repeated model and codec calls may limit deployment (researcher inference).
taxonomy_delta: Image compression/restoration does not map cleanly to the four task labels; retained Unclear while operation and graphics-action relation are explicit.

full_text_reading.limitations_review: No dedicated limitations section; experimental scope and reporting gaps inspected.

papers.canonical_title: Behind Video Generation: Observations and Insights on Multimodal Understanding from Kling
papers.abstract: Technical report on the multimodal understanding stack behind Kling, including captioning, reference-grounded conditioning, prompt enhancement, text encoders, reward modeling and evaluation. Agentic prompt enhancement repairs contradictory story specifications and retrieves compelling examples before basic prompt rewriting.

events.evidence: Official Atom initial timestamp; Chicago 07:56:06 Nov 3.

papers.screening_reason: Agentic PE makes explicit plot, temporal-event and camera-condition decisions that control video generation; Table 13 evaluates its downstream effects. Direct editing of reference media and post-render revision are only experimental extensions, not claimed as deployed.
screening_evidence: 5.4 p.23: refiner reorders, merges or drops events and fixes attributes; retrieves Top-5 examples.
5.5 Table 13 p.24 evaluates cumulative story-refinement and retrieval configurations.
papers.analysis_target: Task-time agentic PE story-refinement/retrieval subsystem of Section 5.4, not basic PE SFT/RL training, caption-production agents, reward-model training or experimental media-editing extensions.

agent_graphics_relation.controller: Agentic PE story refiner and retrieval controller
agent_graphics_relation.action_or_decision: Minimally edits plot events and bindings, retrieves creative captions, supplies authoritative specification to generation conditioning
agent_graphics_relation.graphics_target: Temporal video-generation specification and resulting video through basic PE/DiT
agent_graphics_relation.evidence: Refiner changes event order and attributes; basic PE treats revised prompt as authoritative; controlled video evaluations measure resulting generation.

task.evidence: Refines shot/event progression, performance and camera patterns for video synthesis.
task.reasoning: Temporal content authoring maps most closely to Animation.

input_form.evidence: Agentic PE refines user prompt; references pass unchanged through basic PE.
input_form.reasoning: Text is the demonstrated input of this subsystem; broader multimodal product inputs are not necessarily inspected here.

output.evidence: Output is a user-level specification plus optional context.

model_type.evidence: Shared Kling-MLLM and external baselines are described, but exact deployed agentic refiner backbone is not identified.
model_type.reasoning: Do not transfer basic PE or foundation model architecture to an unspecified agent controller.

model_training.evidence: SFT and RL concern basic PE; joint training of agentic and basic PE is open work.
model_training.reasoning: Agentic PE adaptation is not reported; cannot inherit basic PE training labels.

planning.evidence: Plot plan is revised under three fixed preservation/minimality rules.
planning.reasoning: Explicit temporal plan with generated edits inside fixed refinement/retrieval stages supports PO-2.

workflow.evidence: Story refinement precedes retrieval, then basic PE consumes output.

update_strategy.evidence: Minimal local edits reorder, merge/drop events and fix attributes without new characters.
update_strategy.reasoning: Local Patch acts on the story specification, not pixels.

verifier.evidence: Reasonableness judge and faithfulness checklist check refined output before handoff.
verifier.reasoning: Separate judgment role verifies edits and permits conflict-flag fallback.

feedback_assessment.evidence: Graph conflicts are identified with offending sentence; refiner repairs contradictions or flags unresolved conflict.
feedback_assessment.reasoning: Diagnostic conflict evidence drives edits; training scores and final metrics are not task-time score feedback.

feedback_observation.evidence: Spatial and interaction graphs encode positions, contacts, preconditions and resulting states.
feedback_observation.reasoning: These are structured proposed scene states, not rendered observations; no post-render loop claimed.

memory_time.evidence: Reusable caption index is queried for each refined request.
memory_time.reasoning: Persistent external retrieval memory spans requests; no self-updating experiential memory implied.

memory_reach.evidence: PE retrieval index supplies Top-5 context to its own basic-PE consumer.
memory_reach.reasoning: Scoped PE resource, not global multi-agent memory.

action_type.evidence: Refined plot and optional caption context determine downstream generation condition.
action_type.reasoning: Declarative specification rather than executable code or demonstrated native graphics-tool calls.

graphics_software.evidence: Agentic PE wraps basic PE and text-encoder/DiT conditioning.
graphics_software.reasoning: Agent-facing control layer adapts existing video generator.

tools.evidence: Caption retrieval is described; graphics reference-editing tools are only experimental extensions.
tools.reasoning: No callable graphics operation within the selected subsystem is established; downstream generator is outside this annotation unit.

resources.evidence: Top-5 compelling captions and three hard refinement rules.
resources.reasoning: Captions are Examples & Trajectories; fixed rules are Documentation & Rules.

representation.evidence: Natural-language plot plus spatial/interaction graphs represent proposed video content.
representation.reasoning: Neither prose nor symbolic event graphs maps unambiguously to Code/Layouts/Geometry/Dynamic State; do not inherit downstream pixels.

papers.contribution: Separates creative contradiction repair and retrieval from caption-dialect translation, exposing a practical semantic-control layer for video generation.
papers.limitations: Agentic controller model/adaptation and tool interface are underspecified. Cumulative ablations do not independently isolate every component. Caption retrieval improves vividness but slightly lowers some alignment metrics; generator-in-loop RL reduces creative ceiling. Reference editing, previews and post-generation repair remain ongoing work.
taxonomy_delta: Symbolic temporal plot specifications lack an unambiguous representation label; preserve Unclear rather than treating text as code.
Distinguish task-time graph diagnosis from basic-PE training reward and future visual verification.

papers.canonical_title: Chronos: Sequential Identity-Preserving Video Generation by Temporal Anchoring
papers.abstract: Training-free identity-preserving video generation combines risk-aware prompt adaptation, cascaded visual keyframes and metric-guided selection across heterogeneous generators.
papers.screening_reason: GPT estimates generation risk and chooses visibility/viewpoint interventions that alter video conditioning; explicit metric decisions then select final generated artifacts. Does not require the word agent or autonomous iterative replanning.
screening_evidence: 3.2 p.3: GPT maps generation risks to three intervention levels and generates adapted prompts.
3.4 p.4: weighted routing and failure thresholds determine selected video and human review.
papers.analysis_target: Track 2 task-time temporal anchoring harness: GPT risk-aware conditioning, cascaded anchors and automatic candidate selection; Track 1 is an alternative configuration.

agent_graphics_relation.controller: GPT-based risk-aware prompt controller plus deterministic routing policy
agent_graphics_relation.action_or_decision: Chooses conditioning interventions, cascades identity anchors and selects video candidates
agent_graphics_relation.evidence: Risk score determines prompt intervention; generated keyframes condition video models; evaluation scores determine final artifact.

task.evidence: Sequential action video generation with temporal progression.
task.reasoning: Temporal media generation corresponds to Animation.

input_form.evidence: Reference images, raw prompt and optional temporal captions.

output.evidence: Highest-scoring video is selected as final output.

model_type.evidence: GPT conditions on reference images and text to determine intervention.
model_type.reasoning: Visual-language decision maker, not Hybrid solely because downstream generators are diffusion models.

planning.evidence: Fixed SPA/VFA/MGCR plan follows supplied temporal captions; model changes cues but does not generate an autonomous action plan.
planning.reasoning: PO-1 denotes hard-coded stage/anchor schedule; risk-adaptive content does not establish hybrid planning.

workflow.evidence: Prompt adaptation then cascaded anchors then generator pool and selection.
workflow.reasoning: Fixed sequential stages; concurrent generator execution is not reported.

update_strategy.evidence: Evaluated candidates are selected by weighted score and filtered by critical constraints.

verifier.evidence: LLM holistic evaluation, computed metrics and critical-failure human review.
verifier.reasoning: Separate model judge is Critic; score aggregation/thresholds Programmatic; exceptional acceptance is Human.

feedback_assessment.evidence: Normalized score vector plus critical-metric threshold violations control selection/review.
feedback_assessment.reasoning: Score and Binary influence artifact acceptance; no textual diagnostic repair loop claimed.

feedback_observation.evidence: Video identity, motion, visual quality and text alignment are assessed.

memory_time.evidence: Subsequent keyframes reuse previously generated frames as visual conditions.
memory_time.reasoning: Retained image state crosses calls within one generation.

memory_reach.evidence: Reuse occurs inside the VFA cascade.
memory_reach.reasoning: Local stage memory; no cross-run/global store evidenced.

action_type.evidence: Enhanced prompts and structured VFA instructions specify desired content.
action_type.reasoning: Controller produces declarative generation conditions; exact tool-call protocol not given.

graphics_software.evidence: Temporal anchoring and routing harness wraps GPT image generation, Wan and Seedance.
graphics_software.reasoning: Added control layer adapts existing generators.

tools.evidence: Image/video generators and perceptual assessors are invoked; threshold checker gates review.
tools.reasoning: Generative/analytical models are Perception models per codebook; deterministic gate is Static Validator.

resources.evidence: Structured instruction template S_VFA and fidelity-preserving editing instructions.
resources.reasoning: Reusable instructions are Documentation & Rules; user reference images are task inputs, not retrieved Assets.

representation.evidence: Keyframes and candidate videos carry visual state.

papers.contribution: Combines risk-adjusted semantic conditioning, identity-consistent keyframe cascades and measured selection of complementary video generators.
papers.limitations: No dedicated limitations section. Ablations use only first 100 cases due to high evaluation cost; routing weights and failure thresholds are not detailed. Track 2 motion amplitude is below several baselines, so overall score does not imply uniform improvement. No post-selection autonomous regeneration is demonstrated.

papers.canonical_title: EvoDesign: Agentic Editable Diagram Creation via Design Expertise Evolution
papers.abstract: High-fidelity diagram creation requires coordinated visual-spatial decisions over semantic topology, visual styling, and geometric layout. Existing methods face a representation gap: pixel-based generation offers limited object-level control, while code-based synthesis provides executable structure at the cost of intuitive manipulation. We introduce EvoDesign, an agentic framework for editable diagram creation through an intermediate canvas schema that is both machine-actionable and directly manipulable by users. EvoDesign first constructs a diagram manifest through coordinated structure, style, and layout agents, and then renders the manifest in a diagnostic verification environment. This environment produces objective defect signals and VLM-based critique, enabling localized refinement of the current diagram while also providing evidence for long-term design expertise evolution. The evolution mechanism distills refinement traces into a three-tier design expertise memory, where candidate strategies are linked to the verification evidence that supports them and are promoted into broader guidelines and principles only through repeated cross-context support. We further define CanvasBench, a canvas-recoverable benchmark and evaluation protocol with content, visual, and cognitive dimensions. Experiments across pixel, code-based, agentic, one-shot schema, and canvas-native methods show that EvoDesign provides the strongest overall balance across content fidelity, visual organization, and cognitive usability. Our code is available at https://github.com/GeminiLight/EvoDesign.

papers.canonical_title: WorldAct: Activating Monolithic 3D Worlds into Interactive-Ready Object-Centric Scenes
papers.abstract: Recent 3D world modeling systems based on generative scene synthesis, such as Marble, can create coherent and explorable 3D environments, yet their outputs are typically static monolithic assets with limited editability and physical interaction. This restricts their use in immersive content creation and embodied simulation, where generated worlds must be actively modified and manipulated. To tackle this challenge, we present WorldAct, a framework that converts static generated 3D worlds into editable and interaction-ready scenes. WorldAct uses a multimodal agent to guide scene decomposition, identify actionable objects, reconstruct geometrically aligned object-level meshes for interaction, and restore the residual background via 3D inpainting. The resulting scenes support object-level editing, collision-aware manipulation, and embodied task execution while preserving global scene coherence. Experiments show that WorldAct enables richer interaction scenarios than the original generated scenes, suggesting a practical path toward editable and interactive 3D world models. Project page: https://sjtu-deepvisionlab.github.io/WorldAct

papers.canonical_title: NeoWorld-Pro: Programming Interactive Scenes from Monocular Images for Embodied Simulation
papers.abstract: The advancement of Embodied AI necessitates high-quality simulation assets that faithfully mirror the real world. However, transforming raw visual observations into simulation-ready scenes remains challenging due to the lack of physical grounding and scene-level interactivity in current image-to-URDF methods. We propose NeoWorld-Pro, a framework that reformulates monocular scene reconstruction as procedural programming for interactive 3D environments. Leveraging the zero-shot reasoning and code synthesis capabilities of MLLMs, NeoWorld-Pro converts a single RGB image into executable programs specifying object geometry, articulation, and physical properties. A physics-in-the-loop mechanism then iteratively refines the generated programs by validating their execution in a physics engine, enforcing physically plausible articulations, valid object compositions and interactions, and accurate spatial relationships. Experiments show that NeoWorld-Pro outperforms open-loop and prior monocular reconstruction methods, while enabling complex downstream tasks such as stable stacking and fine-grained manipulation.

papers.canonical_title: FLASH: A "Generate Once, Synthesize Many" Framework for Synthetic Anomaly Generation in Industrial Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: Synthetic anomaly generation helps expand industrial anomaly datasets when real defects are scarce or unavailable. Existing approaches lie at two extremes: procedural approaches are fast but struggle to represent complex anomalies, while generative approaches produce diverse defects but require costly per-sample generation. We present FLASH, a framework that decouples defect generation from anomaly synthesis under a ``generate once, synthesize many'' paradigm. Given only normal images, FLASH uses Vision-Language Model (VLM) guidance and an image-generation model to produce a small set of defect images, from which it extracts, validates, and banks reusable defect patches. For synthesis of anomalous images, Object Boundary Suppression (OBS) first identifies the probable foreground object-aware region of the host image, while Multi-Resolution Spectral Pyramid (MRSP) noise generates diverse, size-controllable masks that determine the defect location and spatial extent. It then composes a large and diverse synthetic anomalous image set by localizing the defect region, sampling size-controllable placement masks and seamlessly blending retrieved defects onto new defect-free images without further need for image generation. Experiments on the MVTec AD 2 dataset show that FLASH-generated anomalies nearly close the calibration gap on real defects, reaching 78.1% image-level F1 against an 83.6% real-anomaly upper bound and providing the most consistent calibration transfer across detectors among procedural and generative alternatives. Moreover, FLASH synthesizes anomalies more than 11.95x faster than per-sample generative approaches.
